newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian Mobitel sees big rise in mobile users.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian Mobitel sees big rise in mobile users.

text.p: Slovenia's unlisted state-owned Mobitel said on Wednesday it expected the number of its mobile phone users to reach 245,000 by the year 2,000, from the current figure of 60,750 users.

The company forecast that the number of GSM phone users would rise to 200,000 in the next three years from 20,000 at present, while the number of analogue mobile phone users would rise to 45,000 from the current 40,750.
Mobitel said it hoped to remain the main mobile phone operator in Slovenia despite the fact that its monopoly is due to expire in 1998 at the latest.

"From the start we were aware that the monopoly did not have a long-term perspective. While we want to keep a leading position we welcome competition which will enhance our efforts to further improve the quality of our services," Mobitel's chief executive Anton Majzelj told a news conference.

The Slovenian Constitutional Courts ruled in July that Mobitel's monopoly was unconstitutional and that other companies should be allowed to use radio frequencies on an equal basis before the government announced a public tender for further concessions in the sector.
According to Slovenia's telecoms law the government must announce a tender by the end of June 1998.
So far three companies -- Digitel, Si.Mobil and Detel 5 -- have shown interest in participating in Slovenia's mobile phone sector.
